summary: Standing 100-foot Price County tower (also Worchester or Phillips), built after 1940 per NHLR; FFLOS lists it standing; no staffing or access sources found.

access.note: No access information in the sources read

events.note: NHLR Built field reads after 1940; the exact year is unknown, so 1940 is a lower bound, not the build year

evidence.quote: Exact construction date is unknown however it was likely after 1940 as the tower was not included in a statewide tower survey dated September 1940.

corrections.why: NHLR says the exact construction date is unknown and the tower was likely built after 1940, since it is absent from a September 1940 statewide survey; 1940 is not supported as the build year

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register calls it Worcester Lookout; the Forest Fire Lookout Association lists it as Worchester (Phillips); the Central US Lookouts site files it under Phillips. The story uses the Register's name and gives the other two.

sources.title: DNR decommissioning all Wisconsin fire towers
Connecting the dots: the fire towers of Wisconsin

notes_for_editor: Brief's 1940 build date is wrong: NHLR says the date is unknown and likely after 1940, so the correction was applied to the story and events. Worcester is not named in the statewide decommissioning sources, and no staffing, fire or access sources were found; the story says so. The Central US Lookouts Phillips page has only a header and a county line, no tower text. The FFLOS and NHLR agree on Price County, standing status and the 100-ft height. WebSearch used twice.
